style: Cinematic and natural: real daylight or practical light, shallow depth of field, subtle handheld, true skin tones, calm pacing. No subtitles, no captions, no on-screen text, no logos, no readable writing anywhere.

clips.p: Sam Patel in a grey hoodie at a suburban kitchen table at 11 pm, laptop glow on his face, a cold mug beside him. He scrolls on the laptop, stops, rubs one eye; the phone on the table buzzes and lights up; he glances at it and sighs. He says quietly and flat: "That's three swaps since dinner." The screens are only a soft glow, nothing readable. Ambience: a clock ticking, a fridge hum.

Emma Walsh in navy scrubs at a bright kitchen fridge in the morning. Her finger runs slowly along a row of an unreadable printed sheet held by a magnet; she turns her head toward the doorway and calls through, fond and unhurried: "Saturday, love. It's on the fridge." Morning kitchen ambience, a kettle.

Morning handover at a nurses' station. A small group of clinicians in scrubs talk quietly; two of them glance at their phones and smile; Sam Patel, at the edge of the group, puts his phone in his pocket and turns back to the conversation. Gentle camera drift, soft department ambience.

One continuous shot, no cuts. Emma Walsh in a denim jacket over a white tee at a café window seat, a flat white beside her, thumb moving on her phone. She lifts her head from the phone and says the line out loud, clearly, her lips moving with every word, a small satisfied nod at the end: "Resus Tuesday… and the Thursday evening. Done." Then she looks back down at the phone. Natural, unhurried movement; morning light.
clips.p_take1_closed_lips: Emma Walsh in a denim jacket at a café window seat with a flat white, thumb on her phone. Two thumb taps, a pause, a small satisfied nod; she picks up the coffee and says half to herself: "Resus Tuesday… and the Thursday evening. Done." The phone screen is only a soft glow. Café ambience, an espresso machine in the background.
clips.note: take 2 (7 Oct): take 1 had her lips closed in a smile through the whole line; the voice of take 2 leads the lips by ~80 ms, so the timeline delays its audio 0.06 s

clips.p: Sam Patel in teal scrubs at the doctors' station, a laptop open with a softly glowing screen, coffee in one hand. He sips, watches the screen, raises an eyebrow and says, dry: "Half full already." Quiet department ambience.

Emma Walsh in navy scrubs steps to the side of a quiet hospital corridor, phone to her ear, listening, one hand on the handrail. She listens, closes her eyes for a beat, exhales, and answers gently: "I'll come and get her. Twenty minutes." Distant corridor ambience.

Close-up of a woman's hands with fair skin holding a phone in a pale corridor, the screen a soft white glow. Two deliberate thumb taps, a short pause, a third; the thumb lifts. Nothing readable on the screen. Quiet corridor ambience.

Alex Campbell beside a commuter bike in a staff car park, black cycling jacket half on over ceil-blue scrubs, reading his phone in bright afternoon light. He reads, grins, taps once, and swings the jacket on, saying to himself, amused: "I'll take your Saturday." Outdoor ambience, birds, distant traffic.

Tracking shot alongside Sam Patel in teal scrubs walking a hospital corridor between two doors, phone raised in one hand, not breaking stride. One tap on the phone without slowing; he says matter-of-fact: "Cover's fine. Approved." Corridor ambience, footsteps.

One continuous shot, no cuts. Morgan O'Brien, 52, reading glasses pushed up, navy blazer, reads a laptop in a small hospital office; Sam Patel in teal scrubs leans in at the door with two takeaway coffees and sets one down. Morgan, not looking up, says: "So that's everyone." Sam answers, speaking clearly with his lips moving on each word, not grinning: "Five rosters. One heading." Quiet office ambience.
clips.p_take1_grin: Morgan O'Brien, a man of 52 with short grey-flecked hair, reading glasses pushed up, a navy blazer over a white open-collar shirt, reading a laptop in a small hospital office with venetian blinds; Sam Patel leaning in at the door holding two takeaway coffees. Morgan scrolls and tilts her head; Sam steps in and sets a coffee down beside her. Morgan, not looking up: "So that's everyone." Sam: "Five rosters. One heading." Quiet office ambience.
clips.note: take 3 (7 Oct): take 1 had Sam grinning through his reply with almost no articulation; a longer two-line prompt failed on Veo (take 2), this shorter one passed; both voices lead the lips by 40-80 ms, so the timeline delays the clip's audio 0.05 s; a Kling take of the same prompt is kept as F10-takeK
clips.p_cups: One continuous shot, no cuts. Morgan O'Brien, 52, reading glasses pushed up, navy blazer, reads a laptop in a small hospital office; Sam Patel in teal scrubs leans in at the door holding two takeaway coffees, one in each hand, and keeps holding both the whole time; nothing is set down, and the desk holds only the laptop and a folder. Morgan, not looking up, says: "So that's everyone." Sam answers, speaking clearly with his lips moving on each word, not grinning: "Five rosters. One heading." Quiet office ambience. clips.note_cups: take 4 (8 Oct): the shipped take ended with Sam back at the door holding two cups while one stayed on the desk (three cups). Two takes with the coffees kept in hand (p_cups): take 1 overlapped the two lines and barely articulated; take 2 (used) sets both cups down and leans in, Sam's line correlates 0.68 with the voice band, audio leads by ~80 ms, so the timeline delays the clip's audio 0.07 s.

clips.p: One continuous shot, no cuts. A back garden at dusk. In the foreground a boy of about ten with his back to the camera holds a football under his arm. Beyond him Sam Patel, in a faded navy polo, sits at the timber outdoor table, looks up at the boy and says easily: "No, I'm done. Round's closed." and stands up, smiling. Slow, natural movement. Warm low sun, evening garden ambience.

clips.p: Slow tracking shot from behind as Emma Walsh and Sam Patel in scrubs walk side by side in through the staff entrance of a hospital at first light, phones in their pockets, mid-conversation, the glass doors sliding open ahead of them onto the light. Dawn ambience, the doors sliding, soft footsteps. No dialogue.

One continuous shot, no cuts. A bright small kitchen at 7 am. Emma Walsh, in plain navy hospital scrubs, slips her phone into her pocket and picks up her car keys from the bench. From the next room a child's voice calls, off camera: "Mum, Saturday?" Emma glances toward the doorway, smiles and answers warmly: "It's in the calendar, love." then heads for the door. The fridge beside her stays bare except a child's drawing under a magnet. Natural, unhurried movement; morning light.
